articles.title: Blue Origin rocket's reusable booster lands but satellite misses orbit
articles.lede: Blue Origin rocket’s reusable booster lands but satellite misses orbit. The New Glenn rocket lifted off at around 7.25am ET from Cape Canaveral, with the booster touchdown coming about 10 minutes later. (AFP pic) CAPE CANAVERAL: The reusable booster of the New Glenn rocket launched from Florida on Sunday by Jeff Bezos' company Blue Origin touched down successfully but the rocket failed to deploy the AST SpaceMobile communications satellite it was carrying into the correct orbit. The launch was the latest chapter in Blue Origin's intensifying rivalry with Elon Musk's SpaceX. The rocket lifted off at around 7.25am ET (1125 GMT) from Cape Canaveral, with the booster touchdown coming about 10 minutes later. New Glenn carried AST's BlueBird 7 satellite to low-Earth orbit.
